analysis.title: Rate Shocks Likely Transitory, But Rebuilding Pipeline Could Take Time (Zillow)
key_insights: Deutsche Bank keeps its Buy rating on Zillow ($Z) but cuts the price target to $40 from $50, based on 12x FY27 EBITDA (multiple unchanged). The stock closed at $33.90 on 4 Nov 2026, near lows last seen in Sept. 2022.
3Q26 results were below DB estimates and the 4Q26 guide came in well below DB and Street expectations, as mortgage rates rose and the housing market weakened.

Mortgage rates rose nearly 100bps from end of June through early October, from the mid-6% range to the mid-7% range, among the sharpest three-month increases since the 1980s. The speed of the move cut conversion for buyers who entered the funnel in July/August.
The industry purchase mortgage outlook moved from a mid-single-digit decline to down 10%-15% y/y in 4Q. Connections normally fall 20%-25% sequentially from 3Q to 4Q before rising in 1Q.

DB expects the rebuild to start with connections in 1Q27 rather than during 4Q, and to turn into transactions around 2Q27. The pipeline needs time because new buyers must enter at current affordability, get pre-approved, find an agent, shop and close.
Residential revenue fell 4% y/y to $419mn in 3Q, including an estimated 600bps drag from the move to Preferred. 4Q guide is a 9%-15% decline, including a 900-1,000bps transition headwind.

Two-thirds of buyer connections went to Preferred partners in 3Q versus about one-third a year ago. DB expects more than 75% by year-end and 100% in 1H27. Preferred connections convert better and generate about 35% more revenue per connection than the legacy advertising model.

Mortgage revenue rose 32% y/y to $70mn in 3Q with purchase originations up 55%, but missed DB's estimate of $80mn as rate volatility cut conversion. 4Q Mortgage revenue is guided down low-single digits despite high-single-digit growth in purchase originations.
The Preferred mortgage channel is expected to grow in the mid-20% range in 4Q against an industry down 10%-15%. Finance First has been hit harder by the rate shock.

Rentals revenue rose 26% y/y to $220mn. Multifamily revenue grew 35% against 17% growth in multifamily properties to a record 81k. DB estimates about half of the growth now comes from monetizing the installed base, versus more than 80% from added properties in the past.
Rentals plus software are approaching 40% of revenue and act as ballast until housing transaction volumes and the connection pipeline recover.
DB cuts 4Q26 revenue to $649mn from $710mn and EBITDA to $118mn (18.2% margin) from $178mn (25% margin). Both are in line with guidance of $635-$665mn revenue and $100-$135mn EBITDA.

DB's FY26/FY27 revenue estimates fall to $2.85bn/$3.17bn from $2.94bn/$3.34bn, versus Street at $2.94bn/$3.28bn. FY26/FY27 EBITDA falls to $674mn/$757mn from $743mn/$988mn, below pre-print consensus of $744mn/$907mn.
DB estimates FY26 diluted EPS at -$0.47 versus +$0.35 previously, and FY27 EPS at $0.83 versus $1.17 previously. FY26 FCF falls to $137mn from $389mn.
Key risks named: regulation, competition from portals and brokers, lack of valuation support, dependence on advertising, risk to new business lines and the dual class share structure.

market_movers.rationale: Target cut to $40 from $50 on lower estimates, valued at 12x FY27 EBITDA. DB sees the near-term weakness as transitory and FY27 as an easier set-up.

sector_views.rationale: Housing transaction volumes are at multi-year troughs and mortgage rates rose sharply. DB expects the timing of normalization to be unclear, with Zillow's pipeline rebuild starting in 1Q27.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported revenue $724mn vs DB estimate $753mn and Street estimate $753mn. It rose 7.1% y/y and the company's guide was $745-$760mn.
3Q26 reported adjusted EBITDA $182mn vs DB estimate $191mn and Street estimate $192mn. Margin was 25.1%. Company guide was $180-$200mn.
3Q26 reported diluted EPS was -$0.70 vs DB estimate $0.06 and Street estimate $0.16. Reported free cash flow was $119mn vs DB estimate $216mn.
3Q26 reported segment revenue: Residential $419mn (DB est $437mn), Mortgages $70mn (DB est $80mn), Rentals $220mn (DB est $222mn).

4Q26 company guidance: revenue $635-$665mn and adjusted EBITDA $100-$135mn. DB estimates are revenue $649mn, EBITDA $118mn and EPS $0.04, against Street estimates of $709mn revenue, $185mn EBITDA and $0.19 EPS before the print.
FY26 company guidance is revenue $2,841-$2,867mn. DB estimates FY26 revenue of $2,853mn (+10.4% y/y), adjusted EBITDA of $674mn and EPS of -$0.47.
DB estimates 1Q27 revenue of $724mn (previously $786mn, Street $773mn) and EBITDA of $190mn (previously $247mn, Street $218mn).

macro_indicators.reading: Mid-7% range, up nearly 100bps from the mid-6% range
macro_indicators.interpretation: A fast rise in mortgage rates cut buyer conversion and reduced housing transaction volumes. It is the main driver of Zillow's weak 4Q26 guide.
macro_indicators.period: End of June to early October 2026

macro_indicators.interpretation: The industry outlook was previously a mid-single-digit decline. The weaker outlook feeds into lower connections and revenue for Zillow.

trade_ideas.description: Buy $Z with a $40 price target (12x FY27 EBITDA)
trade_ideas.rationale: The near-term pipeline damage from the rate shock looks transitory. Revenue growth could reaccelerate as the housing market improves and Preferred completes its rollout.
trade_ideas.risk: Regulation, competition from portals and brokers, lack of valuation support, dependence on advertising, risk to new business lines and dual class share structure.

risk_factors: Further mortgage rate increases or a longer housing downturn could delay the rebuild of the connection pipeline
Preferred transition lowers revenue and EBITDA in the near term and limits visibility

tension_points.bull_case: DB argues the weakness is transitory. As the housing market improves and the pipeline rebuilds, top line growth could reaccelerate, and Preferred connections convert better with about 35% more revenue per connection.
tension_points.bear_case: The rate shock broke the near-term pipeline and rebuilding takes time. Preferred transition creates a revenue and EBITDA headwind with limited visibility, and Zillow's first-time buyer base is highly sensitive to mortgage rates.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A connections recovery that does not begin in 1Q27, or mortgage rates staying in the mid-7% range, would delay the rebuild that DB expects to turn into transactions in 2Q27.

theme_stances.key_argument: The Preferred model ties revenue to transaction value and converts better, so the near-term headwind is transitional rather than a sign of underperformance.
theme_stances.evidence: positive strategic move that aligns Zillow's revenue with its clients

theme_stances.key_argument: The speed of the rise in mortgage rates broke the near-term pipeline, and the rebuild begins with connections in 1Q27.
theme_stances.evidence: The rate shock broke the near-term pipeline, and rebuilding it will take time.
